# Failure-aware evidence fusion

::: {.hub-record-hero .hub-idea-hero}
<p class="hub-idea-status">Idea · High priority · 2/9 readiness fields complete</p>

<p class="hub-takeaway">Use a reliability check to choose which evidence sources should influence each request.</p>
<p>Response and reference evidence help unevenly, so a fixed mixture can hide failures.</p>

<p class="hub-github-issue"><a href="https://github.com/npatta01/trec_mlm_2026/issues/47">Track in GitHub #47</a></p>

<div class="hub-causal-change">Proposed change</div>
<section class="hub-causal-proposed">
<h3>Proposed</h3>
<p>A reliability gate chooses the evidence mixture.</p>
<dl>
<div>
<dt>Known request pattern</dt>
<dd>Use similar historical requests.</dd>
</div>
<div>
<dt>Stable candidate strength</dt>
<dd>Use semantic profiles.</dd>
</div>
<div>
<dt>Response evidence passes checks</dt>
<dd>Use responses or references.</dd>
</div>
</dl>
</section>
<figcaption class="hub-decision-test">Does the adaptive mixture beat the frozen dense/profile control?</figcaption>
</figure>

<p class="hub-next-action">Define and freeze the reliability signal, fallback, and artifact plan.</p>

<details class="hub-details">
<summary>Evidence and current knowledge</summary>
## How does it work?

- Read the new request and estimate which evidence sources are dependable.
- Choose a bounded evidence mixture using the frozen reliability rule.
- Rank candidates and compare with the frozen dense/profile control.

## What do we know?

This is an idea, not a result. It needs a frozen decision rule, named
dependencies, and an artifact plan before it can enter the ready queue.
